newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BOND CURVE FLATTENS SHARPLY AS FUNDS MOVE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BOND CURVE FLATTENS SHARPLY AS FUNDS MOVE.

text.p: The yield curve of Belgian linear bonds flattened sharply on Wednesday as heavy fund selling hit the short end and fund buying lifted the long end despite bullish U.S. retail sales and producer prices.
"We really don't know why they hit the short end so hard today. The dollar is a bit weaker and money rates are fairly stable," one trader said.
"But it is the big boys playing. Final investors are on holiday or just out of the market because of the short week, so the traditional buying support from portfolio managers is missing," he added.

"The curve has flattened a lot today. It was a double impact of selling the short and buying the long. But we can't work out why," another trader said. However, volume was relatively thin and therefore the movements were exaggerated.
"It is very difficult to tell where it will go from here," he added.
The move came despite U.S. July retail sales US-ECI showing consumers returning to the market, and producer prices which dropped for the seventh straight month.
Consumer prices and industrial production are due tomorrow.
July consumer prices are expected to show a rise of 0.2 percent month-on-month and 2.4 percent year-on-year.
June industrial production is expected to show a monthly rise of 0.2 percent.

The yield of the benchmark 10-year Belgian OLO BE286= ended Wednesday at 5.79 percent against Tuesday's closing 5.74 percent, and the spread over German Bunds MEUR ticked in to eight basis points from nine.
The front-month futures contract was 38 basis points off at 120.91, while the one-week repo rate rose to 3.35/40 percent from Tuesday's 3.28/31.
